terms.html: A recurring solution that looks reasonable and reliably causes harm. Publishing them alongside patterns is more effective than either alone, because people recognize their own work faster in a warning than in an ideal.

terms.html: The component that sits in front of APIs handling authentication, routing, rate limiting, and monitoring. Useful, and a magnet for business logic that does not belong there.
terms.text: The component that sits in front of APIs handling authentication, routing, rate limiting, and monitoring. Useful, and a magnet for business logic that does not belong there.

terms.html: A piece of software people interact with directly to do business work. If it only enables other software, it is an IT component, not an application. Where you draw this line matters less than drawing exactly one and applying it everywhere.
terms.text: A piece of software people interact with directly to do business work. If it only enables other software, it is an IT component, not an application. Where you draw this line matters less than drawing exactly one and applying it everywhere.

terms.html: The layer concerned with what applications exist, what each is for, and how they fit together. It is the layer most organizations actually manage, because it is the one with a budget line attached.
terms.text: The layer concerned with what applications exist, what each is for, and how they fit together. It is the layer most organizations actually manage, because it is the one with a budget line attached.

terms.html: The named person in IT accountable for an application's operation, cost, and lifecycle. A team mailbox in the owner field is a record without an owner, however convenient it looks in a report.
terms.text: The named person in IT accountable for an application's operation, cost, and lifecycle. A team mailbox in the owner field is a record without an owner, however convenient it looks in a report.

terms.html: The discipline of knowing what applications you run, what they cost, who owns them, and where they are in their life - and using that knowledge to decide what to invest in, consolidate, or retire.
terms.text: The discipline of knowing what applications you run, what they cost, who owns them, and where they are in their life - and using that knowledge to decide what to invest in, consolidate, or retire.

terms.html: A published, versioned way for one system to ask another for something or tell it something. If it is not published and versioned, it is an internal function call you have decided to depend on.
terms.text: A published, versioned way for one system to ask another for something or tell it something. If it is not published and versioned, it is an internal function call you have decided to depend on.

terms.html: The periodic exercise of asking the portfolio hard questions: why do we run three of these, who still uses this, and what would break if it disappeared. Done continuously it is hygiene; done once a decade it is surgery.

terms.html: An open modelling language for enterprise architecture, with notation for business, application, and technology layers and the relations between them. Precise, learnable, and almost always more notation than your audience wants.
terms.text: An open modelling language for enterprise architecture, with notation for business, application, and technology layers and the relations between them. Precise, learnable, and almost always more notation than your audience wants.

terms.html: The forum where decisions that cross domains get made and recorded. Healthy ones decide few things, quickly, and publish; unhealthy ones review everything and decide nothing.
terms.text: The forum where decisions that cross domains get made and recorded. Healthy ones decide few things, quickly, and publish; unhealthy ones review everything and decide nothing.

terms.html: The informal network of architects across domains and units who share patterns, review each other's work, and keep the practice coherent without a reporting line. In a federation it is not a nice extra, it is the practice.
terms.text: The informal network of architects across domains and units who share patterns, review each other's work, and keep the practice coherent without a reporting line. In a federation it is not a nice extra, it is the practice.

terms.html: A must issued to a project, with a reason, a test, an owner, and an expiry. Not a requirement, because requirements are things a project may trade away against cost and time, and it will.
terms.text: A must issued to a project, with a reason, a test, an owner, and an expiry. Not a requirement, because requirements are things a project may trade away against cost and time, and it will.

terms.html: The idea that architecture assets range from generic industry models to your own specific designs, and that you should reuse from the generic end before inventing at the specific end. Useful as a habit, rarely useful as a diagram.
terms.text: The idea that architecture assets range from generic industry models to your own specific designs, and that you should reuse from the generic end before inventing at the specific end. Useful as a habit, rarely useful as a diagram.

terms.html: A one-page record of a significant decision: the context, the drivers, the options considered, the choice, and its consequences. The cheapest institutional memory an IT organization can buy.
terms.text: A one-page record of a significant decision: the context, the drivers, the options considered, the choice, and its consequences. The cheapest institutional memory an IT organization can buy.

terms.html: The cyclical process at the centre of TOGAF, running from vision through business, application, and technology architecture to migration planning and governance. Read it as a list of questions rather than a sequence of phases.
terms.text: The cyclical process at the centre of TOGAF, running from vision through business, application, and technology architecture to migration planning and governance. Read it as a list of questions rather than a sequence of phases.

terms.html: The set of forums, decision rights, and records through which architecture actually influences outcomes. Governance that arrives at the end is only ever a veto, and a veto is the least useful thing an architect can offer.
terms.text: The set of forums, decision rights, and records through which architecture actually influences outcomes. Governance that arrives at the end is only ever a veto, and a veto is the least useful thing an architect can offer.

terms.html: A short, opinionated rule that decides real trade-offs - "buy before build", "one core system per process step". If a principle has never made anyone unhappy in a review, it is a poster, not a principle.

terms.html: The place where the models, decisions, standards, and inventory actually live and can be queried. If yours is a folder of slide decks, you have documentation rather than a repository.
terms.text: The place where the models, decisions, standards, and inventory actually live and can be queried. If yours is a folder of slide decks, you have documentation rather than a repository.

terms.html: The governance body that checks planned work against the target landscape, standards, and principles. Healthy ones decide little, early, and fast; unhealthy ones become the department of no.
terms.text: The governance body that checks planned work against the target landscape, standards, and principles. Healthy ones decide little, early, and fast; unhealthy ones become the department of no.

terms.html: The short statement of where the landscape is heading and why, written before the detailed work starts. One page that survives contact with a steering committee beats forty that do not.
terms.text: The short statement of where the landscape is heading and why, written before the detailed work starts. One page that survives contact with a steering committee beats forty that do not.

terms.html: Exchange where the sender does not wait for the receiver, using events or queues. It absorbs the gap between a core that is upgrading and a market that is trading, which is why it should be the default.
terms.text: Exchange where the sender does not wait for the receiver, using events or queues. It absorbs the gap between a core that is upgrading and a market that is trading, which is why it should be the default.

terms.html: The periodic confirmation by an owner that a record is still true. The cheapest data quality mechanism there is, and the one whose age tells you more about a repository than any completeness percentage.
terms.text: The periodic confirmation by an owner that a record is still true. The cheapest data quality mechanism there is, and the one whose age tells you more about a repository than any completeness percentage.

terms.html: The immutable record of who did what and when. Cheap to add at design time, impossible to reconstruct afterwards, and always wanted urgently.
terms.text: The immutable record of who did what and when. Cheap to add at design time, impossible to reconstruct afterwards, and always wanted urgently.

terms.html: An isolated failure domain within a cloud region. Spreading across them protects against a data centre failure and not against a bad deployment, which is the failure you are more likely to have.
terms.text: An isolated failure domain within a cloud region. Spreading across them protects against a data centre failure and not against a bad deployment, which is the failure you are more likely to have.

terms.html: The promise that a new version of an interface will not break existing consumers. Every breaking change you avoid is a migration project somebody else does not have to run.
terms.text: The promise that a new version of an interface will not break existing consumers. Every breaking change you avoid is a migration project somebody else does not have to run.

terms.html: The landscape as it is today (baseline) and as it should look at a chosen horizon (target). Everything interesting happens in between - see transition architecture.
terms.text: The landscape as it is today (baseline) and as it should look at a chosen horizon (target). Everything interesting happens in between - see transition architecture.

terms.html: A scheduled bulk exchange rather than a continuous one. Perfectly legitimate, frequently the right answer, and only a problem when nobody can say what happens if a run is missed.
terms.text: A scheduled bulk exchange rather than a continuous one. Perfectly legitimate, frequently the right answer, and only a problem when nobody can say what happens if a run is missed.

terms.html: An approach of choosing the strongest product for each function and integrating them. More capability per function, more integration to own, and the trade-off should be made once and deliberately rather than product by product.
terms.text: An approach of choosing the strongest product for each function and integrating them. More capability per function, more integration to own, and the trade-off should be made once and deliberately rather than product by product.

terms.html: The agreed target design for one domain, covering the process to level three and the systems each step maps to. A blueprint is finished when every step has exactly one target system and every gap has a named owner.
terms.text: The agreed target design for one domain, covering the process to level three and the systems each step maps to. A blueprint is finished when every step has exactly one target system and every gap has a named owner.

terms.html: A programme that converts an existing system and its data into the new one rather than starting over. Cheaper and faster than greenfield, and it carries the old decisions forward whether you inspect them or not.
terms.text: A programme that converts an existing system and its data into the new one rather than starting over. Cheaper and faster than greenfield, and it carries the old decisions forward whether you inspect them or not.

terms.html: The layer that describes what the organization does and how it is organized to do it - capabilities, value streams, processes, and the objects they act on - independent of systems. Done well it is the only architecture business people ever ask to see again.
terms.text: The layer that describes what the organization does and how it is organized to do it - capabilities, value streams, processes, and the objects they act on - independent of systems. Done well it is the only architecture business people ever ask to see again.

terms.html: Something the business must be able to do - "forecast demand", "onboard employees" - independent of who does it, how, or with which system. The most stable vocabulary an enterprise has, which is why maps are drawn with it.
terms.text: Something the business must be able to do - "forecast demand", "onboard employees" - independent of who does it, how, or with which system. The most stable vocabulary an enterprise has, which is why maps are drawn with it.

terms.html: The document that justifies spending money on a change. Architecture's contribution is the impact list with names on it, which is more persuasive than any qualitative paragraph about alignment.
terms.text: The document that justifies spending money on a change. Architecture's contribution is the impact list with names on it, which is more persuasive than any qualitative paragraph about alignment.

terms.html: A rating of how well an application supports the process it exists for, given by the business, not by IT. Separate it from technical fit or you get one blended number that hides which problem you actually have.
terms.text: A rating of how well an application supports the process it exists for, given by the business, not by IT. Separate it from technical fit or you get one blended number that hides which problem you actually have.

terms.html: An organizational grouping of work, usually matching a department. Related to capability but not the same thing, and confusing the two is how capability maps end up mirroring the org chart.
terms.text: An organizational grouping of work, usually matching a department. Related to capability but not the same thing, and confusing the two is how capability maps end up mirroring the org chart.

terms.html: How an organization creates, delivers, and captures value. Architecture that does not know the business model will optimize for the wrong constraint with total confidence.
terms.text: How an organization creates, delivers, and captures value. Architecture that does not know the business model will optimize for the wrong constraint with total confidence.

terms.html: A thing the business recognizes and talks about: an order, a contract, a shipment. The bridge between process design and the data model, and the reason both should be drawn by people who have met.
terms.text: A thing the business recognizes and talks about: an order, a contract, a shipment. The bridge between process design and the data model, and the reason both should be drawn by people who have met.

terms.html: The named person on the business side accountable for what an application is used for and whether it still earns its place. Coverage of this field always trails IT ownership, and reporting the two separately is what makes the gap fixable.
terms.text: The named person on the business side accountable for what an application is used for and whether it still earns its place. Coverage of this field always trails IT ownership, and reporting the two separately is what makes the gap fixable.

terms.html: A sequence of activities producing an outcome for a customer or the organization. Processes cross departments, which is why they are hard to own and why naming one owner matters so much.
terms.text: A sequence of activities producing an outcome for a customer or the organization. Processes cross departments, which is why they are hard to own and why naming one owner matters so much.

terms.html: The single named person accountable for one end-to-end process across all markets and units - its design, its performance, and its exceptions. Where there are two owners, there are zero.
terms.text: The single named person accountable for one end-to-end process across all markets and units - its design, its performance, and its exceptions. Where there are two owners, there are zero.

terms.html: A statement that constrains or drives business behaviour: a credit limit, an approval threshold, an eligibility test. Rules buried in code become organizational folklore, which is why the good ones get written down somewhere a non-developer can read.
terms.text: A statement that constrains or drives business behaviour: a credit limit, an approval threshold, an eligibility test. Rules buried in code become organizational folklore, which is why the good ones get written down somewhere a non-developer can read.

terms.html: Something one part of the organization provides to another with a defined outcome and a service level. Naming them turns internal favours into things that can be measured and, occasionally, improved.
terms.text: Something one part of the organization provides to another with a defined outcome and a service level. Naming them turns internal favours into things that can be measured and, occasionally, improved.

terms.html: A way of describing software architecture at four zoom levels - context, container, component, code - so that each diagram has one audience. Its real contribution is the discipline of not mixing levels on one page.
terms.text: A way of describing software architecture at four zoom levels - context, container, component, code - so that each diagram has one audience. Its real contribution is the discipline of not mixing levels on one page.

terms.html: One agreed shape per business object, used inside the integration layer, with system-specific dialects translated at the edges. Twelve formats at the boundary is fine; twelve dialects inside is a layer nobody can change.
terms.text: One agreed shape per business object, used inside the integration layer, with system-specific dialects translated at the edges. Twelve formats at the boundary is fine; twelve dialects inside is a layer nobody can change.

terms.html: A capability map with a verdict painted on it: each tile colored by maturity, cost, risk, or redundancy. The fastest way to turn an inventory into a leadership conversation.
terms.text: A capability map with a verdict painted on it: each tile colored by maturity, cost, risk, or redundancy. The fastest way to turn an inventory into a leadership conversation.

terms.html: The hierarchical inventory of an organization's business capabilities, usually two to three levels deep. Used to anchor application portfolios, investments, and transformation scopes to something that does not reorganize every year.
terms.text: The hierarchical inventory of an organization's business capabilities, usually two to three levels deep. Used to anchor application portfolios, investments, and transformation scopes to something that does not reorganize every year.

terms.html: An assessment of how well the organization performs a capability, usually on a scale of four or five levels. The scale matters far less than the discipline of writing down what each level looks like before anyone scores anything.

terms.html: Detecting and streaming changes from a database as they happen. A powerful way to build integrations, and a direct dependency on somebody else's internal schema unless carefully bounded.
terms.text: Detecting and streaming changes from a database as they happen. A powerful way to build integrations, and a direct dependency on somebody else's internal schema unless carefully bounded.

terms.html: The structured comparison of a target design against one unit's current way of working: align on the design, identify the gaps, translate every gap into a named change topic. Done with the local team, never to them.
terms.text: The structured comparison of a target design against one unit's current way of working: align on the design, identify the gaps, translate every gap into a named change topic. Done with the local team, never to them.

terms.html: The person accountable for the architecture practice as a whole: the principles, the forums, the standards, and the hiring. The role is one third design, one third politics, and one third refusing things gracefully.
terms.text: The person accountable for the architecture practice as a whole: the principles, the forums, the standards, and the hiring. The role is one third design, one third politics, and one third refusing things gracefully.

terms.html: Coordination where each service reacts to events without a central controller. Scales well, and makes it genuinely hard to answer the question "where is my order right now".
terms.text: Coordination where each service reacts to events without a central controller. Scales well, and makes it genuinely hard to answer the question "where is my order right now".

terms.html: The discipline of keeping a packaged system close to standard so that vendor releases can be taken cheaply, with extensions living outside the upgrade path. Not a coding ban - it converts "no customization" into a design decision with four available answers.

terms.html: Designed to run on cloud infrastructure and to use its elasticity, managed services, and failure model. A meaningful engineering stance and a marketing word, and telling which one you are hearing takes about two questions.
terms.text: Designed to run on cloud infrastructure and to use its elasticity, managed services, and failure model. A meaningful engineering stance and a marketing word, and telling which one you are hearing takes about two questions.

terms.html: Something a stakeholder cares about that the architecture has to answer: cost, resilience, time to market, regulatory exposure. Naming concerns before drawing anything is what stops a diagram from being decorative.
terms.text: Something a stakeholder cares about that the architecture has to answer: cost, resilience, time to market, regulatory exposure. Naming concerns before drawing anything is what stops a diagram from being decorative.

terms.html: Changing a packaged system's behaviour through settings the vendor provided. Always the first thing to try, and a striking share of "impossible" requests turn out to be switched off rather than absent.
terms.text: Changing a packaged system's behaviour through settings the vendor provided. Always the first thing to try, and a striking share of "impossible" requests turn out to be switched off rather than absent.

terms.html: The state of a design actually following the standards and patterns it claimed to. Checked by a test somebody can run alone in five minutes, or it will not be checked at all.
terms.text: The state of a design actually following the standards and patterns it claimed to. Checked by a test somebody can run alone in five minutes, or it will not be checked at all.

terms.html: A specific verification performed at a defined moment, usually inside the definition of done. It belongs with whoever already checks the definition of done, never with an architect who has to remember.
terms.text: A specific verification performed at a defined moment, usually inside the definition of done. It belongs with whoever already checks the definition of done, never with an architect who has to remember.

terms.html: A method where a proposal passes unless someone raises a reasoned objection, rather than requiring active agreement from all. Slower to learn and faster to run than consensus, and it works in rooms where nothing can be mandated.
terms.text: A method where a proposal passes unless someone raises a reasoned objection, rather than requiring active agreement from all. Slower to learn and faster to run than consensus, and it works in rooms where nothing can be mandated.

terms.html: A packaged unit of software with its dependencies, runnable anywhere the runtime exists. It solved the works-on-my-machine problem and created a fleet-management problem, which most organizations consider a good trade.
terms.text: A packaged unit of software with its dependencies, runnable anywhere the runtime exists. It solved the works-on-my-machine problem and created a fleet-management problem, which most organizations consider a good trade.

terms.html: Automated checks that a provider still satisfies what its consumers expect. The cheapest insurance against the class of failure that is only discovered in production by somebody else's team.
terms.text: Automated checks that a provider still satisfies what its consumers expect. The cheapest insurance against the class of failure that is only discovered in production by somebody else's team.

terms.html: Changing vendor objects or the data model inside a packaged system. Not forbidden, but governed: a named approver, an expiry date, and a count read aloud once a quarter, because a prohibition drives it underground.
terms.text: Changing vendor objects or the data model inside a packaged system. Not forbidden, but governed: a named approver, an expiry date, and a count read aloud once a quarter, because a prohibition drives it underground.

terms.html: The mapping between identifiers for the same thing in different systems. Unglamorous, permanent, and the single artifact that decides whether a migration is a weekend or a quarter.
terms.text: The mapping between identifiers for the same thing in different systems. Unglamorous, permanent, and the single artifact that decides whether a migration is a weekend or a quarter.

terms.html: The sequence of interactions a customer has with the organization, viewed from their side rather than ours. It reliably exposes handovers between systems that nobody owns, which is why architects should read them.
terms.text: The sequence of interactions a customer has with the organization, viewed from their side rather than ours. It reliably exposes handovers between systems that nobody owns, which is why architects should read them.

terms.html: Any change to a packaged system beyond configuration. The word covers four very different things - in-app extension, side-by-side, modification, and localization - and treating them as one is how modification counts reach the hundreds.

terms.html: The moment a change goes from prepared to live. Rehearse it, write down who calls the rollback, and know exactly which system is authoritative during the window.
terms.text: The moment a change goes from prepared to live. Rehearse it, write down who calls the rollback, and know exactly which system is authoritative during the window.

terms.html: The layer covering what information the organization holds, who owns it, where it lives, and how it moves. Neglected longest and regretted hardest, because every other layer quietly depends on it.
terms.text: The layer covering what information the organization holds, who owns it, where it lives, and how it moves. Neglected longest and regretted hardest, because every other layer quietly depends on it.

terms.html: A searchable index of the data assets an organization holds, with their descriptions and owners. Excellent at describing what exists; not designed to hold a decision about who owns a thing, which is why it does not replace an object model.
terms.text: A searchable index of the data assets an organization holds, with their descriptions and owners. Excellent at describing what exists; not designed to hold a decision about who owns a thing, which is why it does not replace an object model.

terms.html: The label that says how sensitive a piece of data is and therefore how it must be handled. If eighty per cent of your objects end up in the top tier, the tiering is decorative and saying so once a year fixes it.
terms.text: The label that says how sensitive a piece of data is and therefore how it must be handled. If eighty per cent of your objects end up in the top tier, the tiering is decorative and saying so once a year fixes it.

terms.html: The agreed shape, meaning, quality, and delivery promise for data passing between a producer and a consumer. It turns "the feed changed" from a surprise into a breach of something written down.
terms.text: The agreed shape, meaning, quality, and delivery promise for data passing between a producer and a consumer. It turns "the feed changed" from a surprise into a breach of something written down.

terms.html: A grouping of related data objects under one accountable owner - customer data, product data, financial data. It is the data equivalent of a business domain, and drawing them differently causes years of confusion.
terms.text: A grouping of related data objects under one accountable owner - customer data, product data, financial data. It is the data equivalent of a business domain, and drawing them differently causes years of confusion.

terms.html: A store holding large volumes of raw data in its original form for later processing. Genuinely useful, and reliably becomes a swamp in the absence of an object model and ownership.
terms.text: A store holding large volumes of raw data in its original form for later processing. Genuinely useful, and reliably becomes a swamp in the absence of an object model and ownership.

terms.html: The traceable path of a piece of data from origin through every transformation to its final use. Nobody asks for it until an auditor or a wrong number does, at which point they ask urgently.
terms.text: The traceable path of a piece of data from origin through every transformation to its final use. Nobody asks for it until an auditor or a wrong number does, at which point they ask urgently.

terms.html: An approach that treats data as a product owned by the domains that produce it, with a self-serve platform underneath. A sound organizational idea frequently bought as a technology, which is why it disappoints.

terms.html: A business-level piece of information that flows between systems - the order, the invoice, the position record. Naming the data objects on an interface is what turns an arrow on a diagram into something an architect can verify.
terms.text: A business-level piece of information that flows between systems - the order, the invoice, the position record. Naming the data objects on an interface is what turns an arrow on a diagram into something an architect can verify.

terms.html: The business person accountable for a data object: its definition, its quality thresholds, and who may consume it. Distinct from the steward, who does the maintaining, and both names should be real.
terms.text: The business person accountable for a data object: its definition, its quality thresholds, and who may consume it. Distinct from the steward, who does the maintaining, and both names should be real.

terms.html: A dataset packaged for consumption with a contract, an owner, documentation, and a service level. The word product is doing the work here: it implies somebody is accountable for whether anyone can use it.
terms.text: A dataset packaged for consumption with a contract, an owner, documentation, and a service level. The word product is doing the work here: it implies somebody is accountable for whether anyone can use it.

terms.html: The degree to which data is complete, accurate, consistent, and current enough for the decisions it feeds. Measure it against named decisions, not in the abstract, or you will report percentages nobody acts on.
terms.text: The degree to which data is complete, accurate, consistent, and current enough for the decisions it feeds. Measure it against named decisions, not in the abstract, or you will report percentages nobody acts on.

terms.html: The requirement that certain data physically remain within a jurisdiction. Answerable in four days if you keep object-to-component links, and in six weeks if you do not.
terms.text: The requirement that certain data physically remain within a jurisdiction. Answerable in four days if you keep object-to-component links, and in six weeks if you do not.

terms.html: The person who maintains a data object day to day: its definition, its quality rules, its exceptions. Usually five to ten per cent of an existing job rather than a new role, and drawn from someone who already knows the data.
terms.text: The person who maintains a data object day to day: its definition, its quality rules, its exceptions. Usually five to ten per cent of an existing job rather than a new role, and drawn from someone who already knows the data.

terms.html: A structured store optimized for reporting and analysis, fed from operational systems. Older than the lake, better governed than the lake, and still where most organizations' numbers actually come from.
terms.text: A structured store optimized for reporting and analysis, fed from operational systems. Older than the lake, better governed than the lake, and still where most organizations' numbers actually come from.

terms.html: Where messages go when they cannot be processed. An interface without one loses data silently, which is worse than losing it loudly.
terms.text: Where messages go when they cannot be processed. An interface without one loses data silently, which is worse than losing it loudly.

terms.html: The numbered, searchable record of decisions taken, with dates and reasons. Its second use is the one nobody predicts: mined for repetition, it tells you exactly which principles you are missing.
terms.text: The numbered, searchable record of decisions taken, with dates and reasons. Its second use is the one nobody predicts: mined for repetition, it tells you exactly which principles you are missing.

terms.html: The deliberate retirement of a system: data archived, interfaces re-pointed, contract ended, record closed. The most undervalued discipline in IT - nobody gets promoted for it, and every landscape rots without it.
terms.text: The deliberate retirement of a system: data archived, interfaces re-pointed, contract ended, record closed. The most undervalued discipline in IT - nobody gets promoted for it, and every landscape rots without it.

terms.html: The checklist a piece of work must satisfy before it counts as finished. The architect's favorite lever: put "portfolio records updated" inside it, and data quality stops being a favor.
terms.text: The checklist a piece of work must satisfy before it counts as finished. The architect's favorite lever: put "portfolio records updated" inside it, and data quality stops being a favor.

terms.html: Engineer-level technical governance: solution and domain architects reviewing designs in progress, resolving issues before any formal gate. Where review actually improves things rather than judging them.
terms.text: Engineer-level technical governance: solution and domain architects reviewing designs in progress, resolving issues before any formal gate. Where review actually improves things rather than judging them.

terms.html: A body or role with the right to settle design questions within a scope. Works when the scope is narrow and the person is available; fails when it becomes a committee with a calendar.
terms.text: A body or role with the right to settle design questions within a scope. Works when the scope is narrow and the person is available; fails when it becomes a committee with a calendar.

terms.html: A weekly, engineer-level session where design questions get resolved without ceremony. Most decisions should die here, and a practice where they do not has a bottleneck at the top.
