terms.html: Context handed to a designer that shapes the solution without dictating it: the target architecture, the objects in scope, the pattern that already solves part of this. Its entire value is in arriving before the first sketch.
terms.text: Context handed to a designer that shapes the solution without dictating it: the target architecture, the objects in scope, the pattern that already solves part of this. Its entire value is in arriving before the first sketch.

terms.html: A design that knowingly departs from a standard or principle. Recorded with a reason and an expiry it is governance working; unrecorded it is governance that has stopped.
terms.text: A design that knowingly departs from a standard or principle. Recorded with a reason and an expiry it is governance working; unrecorded it is governance that has stopped.

terms.html: The plan and capability for restoring service after a major failure. Its value is entirely in whether it has been tested this year, not in whether it has been written.
terms.text: The plan and capability for restoring service after a major failure. Its value is entirely in whether it has been tested this year, not in whether it has been written.

terms.html: A slice of the business with one accountable owner, a stable set of core objects, and a target architecture. Draw domains on the capability map, never on the org chart, or a reorganization invalidates every assignment you have made.
terms.text: A slice of the business with one accountable owner, a stable set of core objects, and a target architecture. Draw domains on the capability map, never on the org chart, or a reorganization invalidates every assignment you have made.

terms.html: Architecture practiced at the level of one business domain - commerce, finance, HR - by an architect who knows its processes, systems, and politics by name. The layer where enterprise intentions meet delivery reality.
terms.text: Architecture practiced at the level of one business domain - commerce, finance, HR - by an architect who knows its processes, systems, and politics by name. The layer where enterprise intentions meet delivery reality.

terms.html: The period during which two systems both write the same object, typically while mastership moves from one to the other. Register it as an exception with an expiry date, because a window with no written end has been known to run for two years.
terms.text: The period during which two systems both write the same object, typically while mastership moves from one to the other. Register it as an exception with an expiry date, because a window with no written end has been known to run for two years.

terms.html: Two or more systems doing substantially the same job, usually acquired by different units at different times. Finding them is easy; the hard part is that each one has a happy user base and a sunk investment.
terms.text: Two or more systems doing substantially the same job, usually acquired by different units at different times. Finding them is easy; the hard part is that each one has a happy user base and a sunk investment.

terms.html: Protecting stored data so it is unreadable without a key. Widely mandated, widely enabled, and worth checking whether it also covers backups, which is where it is most often forgotten.
terms.text: Protecting stored data so it is unreadable without a key. Widely mandated, widely enabled, and worth checking whether it also covers backups, which is where it is most often forgotten.

terms.html: Protecting data as it moves between systems. Standard for external traffic and still surprisingly optional on internal flows, which is where a lot of quiet exposure lives.
terms.text: Protecting data as it moves between systems. Standard for external traffic and still surprisingly optional on internal flows, which is where a lot of quiet exposure lives.

terms.html: The date after which a vendor no longer sells or maintains a product at all. Distinct from end of support, and the one that turns a planning problem into an audit finding.
terms.text: The date after which a vendor no longer sells or maintains a product at all. Distinct from end of support, and the one that turns a planning problem into an audit finding.

terms.html: The date after which a vendor stops issuing fixes and security patches. A component past this date inside an active application is the clearest form of technical risk a portfolio can carry.
terms.text: The date after which a vendor stops issuing fixes and security patches. A component past this date inside an active application is the clearest form of technical risk a portfolio can carry.

terms.html: The person responsible for making individual technology decisions add up across an organization. Most of the job is not drawing: it is knowing what already exists, who owns it, and which argument is worth having this quarter.
terms.text: The person responsible for making individual technology decisions add up across an organization. Most of the job is not drawing: it is knowing what already exists, who owns it, and which argument is worth having this quarter.

terms.html: The practice of understanding and shaping how an organization's processes, information, and systems fit together - so that individual decisions add up to a coherent whole instead of an expensive coincidence.
terms.text: The practice of understanding and shaping how an organization's processes, information, and systems fit together - so that individual decisions add up to a coherent whole instead of an expensive coincidence.

terms.html: A centralized integration layer that routes and transforms messages between systems. Fine as plumbing, disastrous as a home for business rules, which is exactly where those rules migrate under deadline pressure.
terms.text: A centralized integration layer that routes and transforms messages between systems. Fine as plumbing, disastrous as a home for business rules, which is exactly where those rules migrate under deadline pressure.

terms.html: Moving a decision up when the current forum cannot settle it. Publish the triggers in advance, because an unpredictable escalation path teaches people to avoid the forum entirely.
terms.text: Moving a decision up when the current forum cannot settle it. Publish the triggers in advance, because an unpredictable escalation path teaches people to avoid the forum entirely.

terms.html: The published set of things a vendor or option is scored against, with weights and written anchors. Anchors written after proposals arrive are not criteria, they are rationalizations.
terms.text: The published set of things a vendor or option is scored against, with weights and written anchors. Anchors written after proposals arrive are not criteria, they are rationalizations.

terms.html: A record that something happened, published for anyone interested. Events decouple systems in a way requests cannot, at the cost of making the overall flow harder to see in one place.
terms.text: A record that something happened, published for anyone interested. Events decouple systems in a way requests cannot, at the cost of making the overall flow harder to see in one place.

terms.html: A style where components communicate primarily by publishing and consuming events. Excellent for resilience and independence, demanding in observability, and unforgiving if nobody defined the event shapes.
terms.text: A style where components communicate primarily by publishing and consuming events. Excellent for resilience and independence, demanding in observability, and unforgiving if nobody defined the event shapes.

terms.html: A registered, time-boxed permission to depart from a rule. The expiry date is the whole mechanism: without one, the exception becomes the new standard within eighteen months.
terms.text: A registered, time-boxed permission to depart from a rule. The expiry date is the whole mechanism: without one, the exception becomes the new standard within eighteen months.

terms.html: The date on which an exception, a bridge, or a temporary arrangement must be reviewed. Thirty seconds to write, and the difference between a three-week dual-write window and a two-year one.
terms.text: The date on which an exception, a bridge, or a temporary arrangement must be reviewed. Thirty seconds to write, and the difference between a three-week dual-write window and a two-year one.

terms.html: Moving data out of source systems, reshaping it, and loading it into a target - usually for reporting. Its variant ELT loads first and transforms in place, which is mostly a question of where you want the compute bill.
terms.text: Moving data out of source systems, reshaping it, and loading it into a target - usually for reporting. Its variant ELT loads first and transforms in place, which is mostly a question of where you want the compute bill.

terms.html: One record in the portfolio repository describing one thing - an application, an interface, a capability - with its owners, lifecycle, and relations. The atom of application portfolio management.
terms.text: One record in the portfolio repository describing one thing - an application, an interface, a capability - with its owners, lifecycle, and relations. The atom of application portfolio management.

terms.html: The review route for pattern-conforming changes: declare conformity, get a spot-check, and silence within a fixed window means consent. Not a loophole - the reward for standardization.
terms.text: The review route for pattern-conforming changes: declare conformity, get a spot-check, and silence within a fixed window means consent. Not a loophole - the reward for standardization.

terms.html: An operating model where architecture work is distributed to domain and solution architects who belong to their units, with a small centre holding principles, standards, and the repository. Usually the better design rather than a compromise you settle for.
terms.text: An operating model where architecture work is distributed to domain and solution architects who belong to their units, with a small centre holding principles, standards, and the repository. Usually the better design rather than a compromise you settle for.

terms.html: Integration by placing a file somewhere and hoping. It becomes an interface the moment it has a schema, an owner, monitoring, and dead-letter handling; until then it is the longest-surviving liability in most landscapes.
terms.text: Integration by placing a file somewhere and hoping. It becomes an interface the moment it has a schema, an owner, monitoring, and dead-letter handling; until then it is the longest-surviving liability in most landscapes.

terms.html: Comparing a standard process against how a unit works today and recording every difference. Its output should be a list with routes attached, because a gap with no route becomes an escalation.
terms.text: Comparing a standard process against how a unit works today and recording every difference. Its output should be a list with routes attached, because a gap with no route becomes an escalation.

terms.html: How completely an application covers the functions its users need, independent of how well it runs. Low functional fit is the reliable predictor of the spreadsheet growing next to it.
terms.text: How completely an application covers the functions its users need, independent of how well it runs. Low functional fit is the reliable predictor of the spreadsheet growing next to it.

terms.html: A checkpoint where work must show something specific before proceeding - a direction before design, a sound design before build. Two well-placed gates outperform five badly placed ones, every time.
terms.text: A checkpoint where work must show something specific before proceeding - a direction before design, a sound design before build. Two well-placed gates outperform five badly placed ones, every time.

terms.html: The date a system starts being used for real work. Everything an architect wanted to influence had to be settled well before it, which is the whole argument for arriving early.
terms.text: The date a system starts being used for real work. Everything an architect wanted to influence had to be settled well before it, which is the whole argument for arriving early.

terms.html: The single reconciled version of a master data entity, assembled from several sources. A sensible fallback when no system can be made the master, and a poor substitute for deciding which one should be.
terms.text: The single reconciled version of a master data entity, assembled from several sources. A sensible fallback when no system can be made the master, and a poor substitute for deciding which one should be.

terms.html: A non-negotiable design principle fixed for one process domain - "one position record drives everything". Local exceptions may vary; the golden rule survives all of them.
terms.text: A non-negotiable design principle fixed for one process domain - "one position record drives everything". Local exceptions may vary; the golden rule survives all of them.

terms.html: A programme that builds the new system fresh, with no data or configuration carried over. Clean, slow, and the only honest option when the existing configuration is the problem.
terms.text: A programme that builds the new system fresh, with no data or configuration carried over. Clean, slow, and the only honest option when the existing configuration is the problem.

terms.html: A constraint that keeps teams safe at speed instead of stopping them for inspection - pre-approved patterns, platform defaults, paved roads. The more guardrails, the fewer gates you need.
terms.text: A constraint that keeps teams safe at speed instead of stopping them for inspection - pre-approved patterns, platform defaults, paved roads. The more guardrails, the fewer gates you need.

terms.html: Designing so that a component failure does not take the service down. Costs roughly what people expect; the surprise is the operational complexity, not the infrastructure bill.
terms.text: Designing so that a component failure does not take the service down. Costs roughly what people expect; the surprise is the operational complexity, not the infrastructure bill.

terms.html: A local requirement that exists because it has always existed, often because a system in an earlier decade could not do it another way. The largest of the three localization buckets, and the one that shrinks fastest when you demonstrate the standard with the market's own data.
terms.text: A local requirement that exists because it has always existed, often because a system in an earlier decade could not do it another way. The largest of the three localization buckets, and the one that shrinks fastest when you demonstrate the standard with the market's own data.

terms.html: An integration topology where systems connect to a central hub rather than to each other. Fewer connections to manage, one thing that can take everything down, and a hub that quietly accumulates logic.
terms.text: An integration topology where systems connect to a central hub rather than to each other. Fewer connections to manage, one thing that can take everything down, and a hub that quietly accumulates logic.

terms.html: Running workloads across both owned infrastructure and public cloud. Usually the honest description of where an enterprise actually is rather than a strategy anyone chose.
terms.text: Running workloads across both owned infrastructure and public cloud. Usually the honest description of where an enterprise actually is rather than a strategy anyone chose.

terms.html: The heightened support period immediately after go-live. It is also the last moment anyone will willingly update the repository, which is why the closure checklist belongs here rather than later.
terms.text: The heightened support period immediately after go-live. It is also the last moment anyone will willingly update the repository, which is why the closure checklist belongs here rather than later.

terms.html: The property that processing the same message twice has the same effect as processing it once. Unglamorous, and the difference between a bad night and a boring morning.
terms.text: The property that processing the same message twice has the same effect as processing it once. Unglamorous, and the difference between a bad night and a boring morning.

terms.html: The systems and processes controlling who is who and what they may do. The one platform decision that touches every application, which is why it deserves an architect's attention early.
terms.text: The systems and processes controlling who is who and what they may do. The one platform decision that touches every application, which is why it deserves an architect's attention early.

terms.html: The list of what a proposed change touches: applications, interfaces, objects, components, markets, and open exceptions. A list with names on it beats a forty-page document, and takes a fortieth of the effort.
terms.text: The list of what a proposed change touches: applications, interfaces, objects, components, markets, and open exceptions. A list with names on it beats a forty-page document, and takes a fortieth of the effort.

terms.html: Added fields and logic at extension points the vendor anticipated, using released interfaces. Cheap, close to the data, upgrade-safe, and bounded by what the vendor imagined you might want.
terms.text: Added fields and logic at extension points the vendor anticipated, using released interfaces. Cheap, close to the data, upgrade-safe, and bounded by what the vendor imagined you might want.

terms.html: A published capability or process model for a sector, offered as a starting point rather than an answer. Worth an afternoon of borrowing structure and a firm refusal to adopt wholesale.
terms.text: A published capability or process model for a sector, offered as a starting point rather than an answer. Worth an afternoon of borrowing structure and a firm refusal to adopt wholesale.

terms.html: Renting compute, storage, and networking rather than owning it. You still operate everything above the hypervisor, which is the part people forget when comparing costs.
terms.text: Renting compute, storage, and networking rather than owning it. You still operate everything above the hypervisor, which is the part people forget when comparing costs.

terms.html: The point where a piece of work first becomes visible to the organization. Add five fields here and architecture arrives early for free; miss it and you arrive after the contract.
terms.text: The point where a piece of work first becomes visible to the organization. Add five fields here and architecture arrives early for free; miss it and you arrive after the contract.

terms.html: A cluster of interfaces connecting two major parts of the landscape, such as the ERP core and the commerce stack. Reviewed as a whole, because individual interfaces lie about systemic complexity.
terms.text: A cluster of interfaces connecting two major parts of the landscape, such as the ERP core and the commerce stack. Reviewed as a whole, because individual interfaces lie about systemic complexity.

terms.html: Hosted integration tooling offered as a subscription. Removes the infrastructure problem and leaves the governance problem completely untouched.
terms.text: Hosted integration tooling offered as a subscription. Removes the infrastructure problem and leaves the governance problem completely untouched.

terms.html: A connection over which two systems exchange data objects. The true unit of landscape complexity: applications are what you pay for, interfaces are what you suffer for.
terms.text: A connection over which two systems exchange data objects. The true unit of landscape complexity: applications are what you pay for, interfaces are what you suffer for.

terms.html: The list of what you actually run, with owners and lifecycle states. It is the deliverable, not the report generated from it, and the difference matters six months later.
terms.text: The list of what you actually run, with owners and lifecycle states. It is the deliverable, not the report generated from it, and the difference matters six months later.

terms.html: Software or infrastructure that enables other software - middleware, databases, runtimes - rather than serving business users directly. Kept separate from applications so the portfolio counts things one way.
terms.text: Software or infrastructure that enables other software - middleware, databases, runtimes - rather than serving business users directly. Kept separate from applications so the portfolio counts things one way.

terms.html: The failure mode where architecture produces models nobody uses and judgements nobody asked for. The cure is not more communication, it is doing work that somebody would notice the absence of.
terms.text: The failure mode where architecture produces models nobody uses and judgements nobody asked for. The cure is not more communication, it is doing work that somebody would notice the absence of.

terms.html: The framing that customers hire a product to make progress on something, rather than buying features. A useful antidote in requirement workshops where the list of wanted features has grown longer than the reason for wanting them.
terms.text: The framing that customers hire a product to make progress on something, rather than buying features. A useful antidote in requirement workshops where the list of wanted features has grown longer than the reason for wanting them.

terms.html: A measurable outcome that shows an objective is being met. Architecture mandates land here, in the receiving team's plan, or they do not land at all.
terms.text: A measurable outcome that shows an objective is being met. Architecture mandates land here, in the receiving team's plan, or they do not land at all.

terms.html: The full population of applications, components, and interfaces an organization operates, seen as one system. The thing enterprise architects draw, measure, and slowly bend toward intention.
terms.text: The full population of applications, components, and interfaces an organization operates, seen as one system. The thing enterprise architects draw, measure, and slowly bend toward intention.

terms.html: A picture of part of the landscape at one moment, generated from the inventory rather than drawn by hand. Hand-drawn landscapes are beautiful and wrong within a quarter.
terms.text: A picture of part of the landscape at one moment, generated from the inventory rather than drawn by hand. Hand-drawn landscapes are beautiful and wrong within a quarter.

terms.html: Granting the minimum access needed to do the job. Easy to state, hard to sustain, and the entropy runs one direction unless somebody reviews entitlements on a schedule.
terms.text: Granting the minimum access needed to do the job. Easy to state, hard to sustain, and the entropy runs one direction unless somebody reviews entitlements on a schedule.

terms.html: Where a system stands on its journey: planned, active, phase-out, retired. The single field whose neglect creates zombie applications that appear in budgets but not in anyone's plans.
terms.text: Where a system stands on its journey: planned, active, phase-out, retired. The single field whose neglect creates zombie applications that appear in budgets but not in anyone's plans.

terms.html: The place where statutory and regulatory variations live, built once per requirement rather than once per market. Skipping it is how a legal requirement becomes twelve separately maintained copies.
terms.text: The place where statutory and regulatory variations live, built once per requirement rather than once per market. Skipping it is how a legal requirement becomes twelve separately maintained copies.

terms.html: Recording what a system did, in a form somebody can search later. Frequently treated as disproportionate for small internal flows, right up until the audit that needs exactly those flows.
terms.text: Recording what a system did, in a form somebody can search later. Frequently treated as disproportionate for small internal flows, right up until the audit that needs exactly those flows.

terms.html: A decision that becomes work in somebody's plan. Architecture mandates that do not turn into a receiving team's key results are correspondence, not governance.
terms.text: A decision that becomes work in somebody's plan. Architecture mandates that do not turn into a receiving team's key results are correspondence, not governance.

terms.html: A country or regional unit with its own operations, and usually its own systems and legal constraints. Central architecture that has never visited one will design something the markets route around politely.
terms.text: A country or regional unit with its own operations, and usually its own systems and legal constraints. Central architecture that has never visited one will design something the markets route around politely.

terms.html: The data everything else refers to - customers, products, suppliers, employees. Whoever fails to govern it pays for the failure in every system, every report, and every integration, forever.
terms.text: The data everything else refers to - customers, products, suppliers, employees. Whoever fails to govern it pays for the failure in every system, every report, and every integration, forever.

terms.html: The capability, and usually the platform, for keeping master data consistent across systems. Buying it before deciding which system masters each object gives you a very capable way to synchronize a disagreement.
terms.text: The capability, and usually the platform, for keeping master data consistent across systems. Buying it before deciding which system masters each object gives you a very capable way to synchronize a disagreement.

terms.html: Middleware that accepts messages from producers and delivers them to consumers, with buffering and retry. The component that makes asynchronous integration practical rather than theoretical.
terms.text: Middleware that accepts messages from producers and delivers them to consumers, with buffering and retry. The component that makes asynchronous integration practical rather than theoretical.

terms.html: Data about data: what a field means, where it came from, when it was last changed, who may see it. The layer that makes everything else searchable, and the first thing dropped when a project runs late.
terms.text: Data about data: what a field means, where it came from, when it was last changed, who may see it. The layer that makes everything else searchable, and the first thing dropped when a project runs late.

terms.html: A small, independently deployable service owning one capability. Buys team autonomy at the cost of operational and integration complexity, and it is a poor first move for an organization that has not yet mastered either.
terms.text: A small, independently deployable service owning one capability. Buys team autonomy at the cost of operational and integration complexity, and it is a poor first move for an organization that has not yet mastered either.

terms.html: Software that sits between applications and moves data between them. Keep it thin - routing, transformation, protocol, retry, monitoring - because business rules placed here become a third system with no owner and no tests.
terms.text: Software that sits between applications and moves data between them. Keep it thin - routing, transformation, protocol, retry, monitoring - because business rules placed here become a third system with no owner and no tests.

terms.html: Moving data, users, or workload from one system to another. The estimate is always wrong in the same direction, and the reason is almost always the data rather than the code.
terms.text: Moving data, users, or workload from one system to another. The estimate is always wrong in the same direction, and the reason is almost always the data rather than the code.

terms.html: The smallest version of something that produces real learning in real use. Frequently used as a synonym for "phase one of a fixed plan", which is not the same thing and does not produce learning.
terms.text: The smallest version of something that produces real learning in real use. Frequently used as a synonym for "phase one of a fixed plan", which is not the same thing and does not produce learning.

terms.html: A single deployable application with strictly enforced internal boundaries. Most of the design benefit of microservices with a fraction of the operational cost, and an unfashionable answer that is often the right one.
terms.text: A single deployable application with strictly enforced internal boundaries. Most of the design benefit of microservices with a fraction of the operational cost, and an unfashionable answer that is often the right one.

terms.html: Watching known signals to tell whether a system is healthy. Distinct from observability, which is about answering questions you did not anticipate.
terms.text: Watching known signals to tell whether a system is healthy. Distinct from observability, which is about answering questions you did not anticipate.

terms.html: A single deployable application containing most of a system's functionality. Not a slur: a well-structured monolith outperforms a badly split set of services on almost every dimension that matters.
terms.text: A single deployable application containing most of a system's functionality. Not a slur: a well-structured monolith outperforms a badly split set of services on almost every dimension that matters.

terms.html: Using more than one cloud provider. Sometimes a deliberate resilience or negotiation strategy, more often the accumulated result of independent decisions nobody has reconciled.
terms.text: Using more than one cloud provider. Sometimes a deliberate resilience or negotiation strategy, more often the accumulated result of independent decisions nobody has reconciled.

terms.html: One instance of software serving several customers or units with logical separation. Cheaper to run and unforgiving of isolation bugs, which is why the model should be an explicit decision rather than an implementation detail.
terms.text: One instance of software serving several customers or units with logical separation. Cheaper to run and unforgiving of isolation bugs, which is why the model should be an explicit decision rather than an implementation detail.

terms.html: One page per domain object holding its definition, boundary, owner, master system, key attributes, and links. The unit that turns a data strategy from prose into something the repository can hold.
terms.text: One page per domain object holding its definition, boundary, owner, master system, key attributes, and links. The unit that turns a data strategy from prose into something the repository can hold.

terms.html: A goal-setting method pairing a qualitative objective with measurable results. Useful to architecture mainly as the place where a board decision becomes somebody's quarter.
terms.text: A goal-setting method pairing a qualitative objective with measurable results. Useful to architecture mainly as the place where a board decision becomes somebody's quarter.

terms.html: The ability to understand a system's internal state from what it emits - logs, metrics, traces. The property that decides whether an incident takes twenty minutes or a weekend.
terms.text: The ability to understand a system's internal state from what it emits - logs, metrics, traces. The property that decides whether an incident takes twenty minutes or a weekend.

terms.html: The condition of running technology the market has moved past, whether or not it still works. It rarely causes an outage on its own; it causes a shortage of people willing to touch it.
terms.text: The condition of running technology the market has moved past, whether or not it still works. It rarely causes an outage on its own; it causes a shortage of people willing to touch it.

terms.html: A formal description of concepts and the relationships between them in a domain. Powerful, expensive, and almost always more precision than the argument you are trying to settle requires.
terms.text: A formal description of concepts and the relationships between them in a domain. Powerful, expensive, and almost always more precision than the argument you are trying to settle requires.

terms.html: A standard, machine-readable description of a REST API. Its practical value is that documentation, client code, and tests can all be generated from one file that cannot silently drift.
terms.text: A standard, machine-readable description of a REST API. Its practical value is that documentation, client code, and tests can all be generated from one file that cannot silently drift.

terms.html: How an organization actually runs: its processes, decision rights, roles, and the systems underneath them. Strategy states intent; the operating model is what customers and employees experience.
terms.text: How an organization actually runs: its processes, decision rights, roles, and the systems underneath them. Strategy states intent; the operating model is what customers and employees experience.

terms.html: Coordination where a central component directs the steps of a process across services. Easier to reason about than choreography, and it creates a component that knows too much.
terms.text: Coordination where a central component directs the steps of a process across services. Easier to reason about than choreography, and it creates a component that knows too much.

terms.html: An entry in the repository with no owner, no capability, and no relationships. Usually created during a collection exercise and never completed, and the leading indicator of a repository sliding back into a list.
terms.text: An entry in the repository with no owner, no capability, and no relationships. Usually created during a collection exercise and never completed, and the leading indicator of a repository sliding back into a list.

terms.html: Software bought rather than built, configured to your needs. The trade is a worse fit in exchange for a supported product and somebody else's roadmap, and it is a good trade far more often than engineers like to admit.
terms.text: Software bought rather than built, configured to your needs. The trade is a worse fit in exchange for a supported product and somebody else's roadmap, and it is a good trade far more often than engineers like to admit.

terms.html: A reusable design decision for a recurring problem, with its context, its costs, and its limits stated. If it cannot be wrong in some context, it is a principle; if compliance is a yes or no with no design left, it is a standard.
terms.text: A reusable design decision for a recurring problem, with its context, its costs, and its limits stated. If it cannot be wrong in some context, it is a principle; if compliance is a yes or no with no design left, it is a standard.

terms.html: The catalog of pre-approved ways to solve recurring design problems - the standard integration, the blessed stack, the reference deployment. Its thickness determines how much of your governance can be a fast lane.
terms.text: The catalog of pre-approved ways to solve recurring design problems - the standard integration, the blessed stack, the reference deployment. Its thickness determines how much of your governance can be a fast lane.

terms.html: An authorized attempt to break into a system to find weaknesses. Its value depends entirely on whether the findings get fixed, and the fix rate is the number worth reporting.
terms.text: An authorized attempt to break into a system to find weaknesses. Its value depends entirely on whether the findings get fixed, and the fix rate is the number worth reporting.

terms.html: Any information relating to an identifiable person. Its handling is set by law rather than by architecture, which makes it one of the few constraints where the correct architectural response is to ask a lawyer.
terms.text: Any information relating to an identifiable person. Its handling is set by law rather than by architecture, which makes it one of the few constraints where the correct architectural response is to ask a lawyer.

terms.html: A limited live deployment used to test an approach before wider rollout. A pilot with no defined stop criteria is just an early wave with better public relations.
terms.text: A limited live deployment used to test an approach before wider rollout. A pilot with no defined stop criteria is just an early wave with better public relations.

terms.html: Shared capability offered to internal teams as a service: compute, identity, integration, data. A platform nobody chose to use is an internal monopoly, and it will be judged like one.
terms.text: Shared capability offered to internal teams as a service: compute, identity, integration, data. A platform nobody chose to use is an internal monopoly, and it will be judged like one.

terms.html: A managed environment for running applications without operating the underlying infrastructure. Faster to start, with constraints that only become apparent once you need something the platform did not anticipate.
terms.text: A managed environment for running applications without operating the underlying infrastructure. Faster to start, with constraints that only become apparent once you need something the platform did not anticipate.

terms.html: A direct connection between two systems with no shared contract. Not a sin in itself; the absence of a contract is the sin, and the count of them is what turns a landscape into a fragile web.
terms.text: A direct connection between two systems with no shared contract. Not a sin in itself; the absence of a contract is the sin, and the count of them is what turns a landscape into a fragile web.

terms.html: The set of projects and programmes an organization has chosen to fund. Distinct from the application portfolio, and the two are argued about in different rooms by different people, which is a recurring source of confusion.
terms.text: The set of projects and programmes an organization has chosen to fund. Distinct from the application portfolio, and the two are argued about in different rooms by different people, which is a recurring source of confusion.

terms.html: The measured health of the inventory itself: completeness, ownership coverage, staleness, contradictions. Report it monthly with the specific items rather than the totals, or nothing gets fixed.
terms.text: The measured health of the inventory itself: completeness, ownership coverage, staleness, contradictions. Report it monthly with the specific items rather than the totals, or nothing gets fixed.

terms.html: Three depths of process description: the end-to-end domain (L1), its major subprocesses (L2), and concrete activity steps (L3). Design workshops stop at L3 - below that lives implementation detail.
terms.text: Three depths of process description: the end-to-end domain (L1), its major subprocesses (L2), and concrete activity steps (L3). Design workshops stop at L3 - below that lives implementation detail.

terms.html: Reconstructing how a process actually runs from the event logs the systems already produce. Frequently uncomfortable, because the real process has variants nobody documented and shortcuts nobody admitted.
terms.text: Reconstructing how a process actually runs from the event logs the systems already produce. Frequently uncomfortable, because the real process has variants nobody documented and shortcuts nobody admitted.

terms.html: A coordinated set of projects pursuing one outcome. Programmes exist to manage dependencies; when they exist mainly to manage reporting, delivery slows and nobody can say why.
terms.text: A coordinated set of projects pursuing one outcome. Programmes exist to manage dependencies; when they exist mainly to manage reporting, delivery slows and nobody can say why.

terms.html: The function that runs the delivery lifecycle, its gates, and its reporting. Architecture should attach to what the PMO already runs rather than build a parallel process, and should let the PMO own enforcement.
terms.text: The function that runs the delivery lifecycle, its gates, and its reporting. Architecture should attach to what the PMO already runs rather than build a parallel process, and should let the PMO own enforcement.

terms.html: A time-boxed experiment answering one specific technical question. If it cannot be thrown away, it was not a proof of concept, it was the first release.
terms.text: A time-boxed experiment answering one specific technical question. If it cannot be thrown away, it was not a proof of concept, it was the first release.

terms.html: A pattern where producers emit events without knowing who consumes them. It lets you add a consumer without touching the producer, which over five years is worth more than almost any other integration property.
terms.text: A pattern where producers emit events without knowing who consumes them. It lets you add a consumer without touching the producer, which over five years is worth more than almost any other integration property.

terms.html: A repository mechanism that marks a record as verified by its owner - and breaks visibly when the record changes or ages without review. Broken seals trending down is a portfolio getting healthier.
terms.text: A repository mechanism that marks a record as verified by its owner - and breaks visibly when the record changes or ages without review. Broken seals trending down is a portfolio getting healthier.

terms.html: A change that can start now, with no dependency on a rollout or a restructuring. Quick wins buy the credibility that roadmap items spend.
terms.text: A change that can start now, with no dependency on a rollout or a restructuring. Quick wins buy the credibility that roadmap items spend.

terms.html: A matrix assigning who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed. Rarely remembered; four sentences about who can say no are remembered.
terms.text: A matrix assigning who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed. Rarely remembered; four sentences about who can say no are remembered.

terms.html: The maximum data loss acceptable, expressed as a period of time. Argue about this number before the incident, because during one everybody wants zero.
terms.text: The maximum data loss acceptable, expressed as a period of time. Argue about this number before the incident, because during one everybody wants zero.

terms.html: The maximum acceptable time to restore service after a failure. Frequently stated aspirationally in a policy and never tested against the architecture that has to deliver it.
terms.text: The maximum acceptable time to restore service after a failure. Frequently stated aspirationally in a policy and never tested against the architecture that has to deliver it.

terms.html: Improving the internal structure of code or a system without changing what it does. Continuous refactoring is maintenance; deferred refactoring becomes a project with a business case nobody wants to write.
terms.text: Improving the internal structure of code or a system without changing what it does. Continuous refactoring is maintenance; deferred refactoring becomes a project with a business case nobody wants to write.

terms.html: The worked-out target design for one recurring problem class - data platforms, omnichannel, integration - that individual projects instantiate instead of reinventing. Opinionated by design, or it decides nothing.
terms.text: The worked-out target design for one recurring problem class - data platforms, omnichannel, integration - that individual projects instantiate instead of reinventing. Opinionated by design, or it decides nothing.

terms.html: The small, slow-changing lists everything else uses: country codes, currencies, units, statuses. Trivial until two systems disagree about what "active" means, at which point it is not trivial at all.
terms.text: The small, slow-changing lists everything else uses: country codes, currencies, units, statuses. Trivial until two systems disagree about what "active" means, at which point it is not trivial at all.

terms.html: A geographic location where a cloud provider runs infrastructure. The unit that data residency requirements are actually expressed in, which is why the object-to-component link is worth keeping.
terms.text: A geographic location where a cloud provider runs infrastructure. The unit that data residency requirements are actually expressed in, which is why the object-to-component link is worth keeping.

terms.html: An interface the vendor or team has published, versioned, and promised to keep compatible. Building on anything else means depending on an internal you were never meant to see.
terms.text: An interface the vendor or team has published, versioned, and promised to keep compatible. Building on anything else means depending on an internal you were never meant to see.

terms.html: The ability to re-process messages from a point in time. The recovery mechanism you never budget for and always want at 3am.
terms.text: The ability to re-process messages from a point in time. The recovery mechanism you never budget for and always want at 3am.

terms.html: The system of record for architecture information: applications, components, capabilities, objects, and the relations between them. A spreadsheet is a legitimate repository in year one, as long as the IDs are stable.
terms.text: The system of record for architecture information: applications, components, capabilities, objects, and the relations between them. A spreadsheet is a legitimate repository in year one, as long as the IDs are stable.

terms.html: Synchronous exchange where the caller waits for an answer. Correct when a person is waiting, and a coupling you feel in every maintenance window when they are not.
terms.text: Synchronous exchange where the caller waits for an answer. Correct when a person is waiting, and a coupling you feel in every maintenance window when they are not.

terms.html: An early market survey to understand what is available before defining requirements. Cheap, underused, and the right moment to learn that the category you assumed exists does not.
terms.text: An early market survey to understand what is available before defining requirements. Cheap, underused, and the right moment to learn that the category you assumed exists does not.

terms.html: The formal document inviting vendors to bid. On the buy path this is the last moment architecture has real leverage, which is why involvement after the shortlist is a recovery exercise rather than a review.
terms.text: The formal document inviting vendors to bid. On the buy path this is the last moment architecture has real leverage, which is why involvement after the shortlist is a recovery exercise rather than a review.

terms.html: How long data is kept before it must be deleted or archived, usually set per jurisdiction. Attach it to the object rather than to the systems, and one edit generates the list of forty systems in scope.
terms.text: How long data is kept before it must be deleted or archived, usually set per jurisdiction. Attach it to the object rather than to the systems, and one edit generates the list of forty systems in scope.

terms.html: The sequenced plan that turns a target architecture into waves of funded, owned work. Every item carries an owner, a dependency, and a value statement - a target without a date is a wish.
terms.text: The sequenced plan that turns a target architecture into waves of funded, owned work. Every item carries an owner, a dependency, and a value statement - a target without a date is a wish.

terms.html: Granting permissions to roles and assigning people to roles. Scales far better than per-person grants, and degrades over years as roles accumulate permissions nobody removes.
terms.text: Granting permissions to roles and assigning people to roles. Scales far better than per-person grants, and degrades over years as roles accumulate permissions nobody removes.

terms.html: The prepared route back to the previous state if a change fails. A rollback that has never been tested is a paragraph, not a plan.
terms.text: The prepared route back to the previous state if a change fails. A rollback that has never been tested is a paragraph, not a plan.

terms.html: A group of markets or units that go live together. Waves make multi-year programmes survivable: while one lands, the next is being designed and the last is in hypercare.
terms.text: A group of markets or units that go live together. Waves make multi-year programmes survivable: while one lands, the next is being designed and the last is in hypercare.

terms.html: The split between what it costs to keep a system operating and what it costs to change it. Portfolios that only track the first number always over-invest in the wrong systems.
terms.text: The split between what it costs to keep a system operating and what it costs to change it. Portfolios that only track the first number always over-invest in the wrong systems.

terms.html: A pattern for managing a transaction that spans several services, using compensating actions instead of a distributed lock. Conceptually clean, operationally demanding, and worth it only when the alternative is worse.
terms.text: A pattern for managing a transaction that spans several services, using compensating actions instead of a distributed lock. Conceptually clean, operationally demanding, and worth it only when the alternative is worse.

terms.html: The formal structure of a dataset or message: fields, types, and constraints. A file transfer without one is not an interface, it is a rumour.
terms.text: The formal structure of a dataset or message: fields, types, and constraints. A file transfer without one is not an interface, it is a rumour.

terms.html: The boundary between two domains where responsibility is genuinely contested - the invoice, consent, stock in transit. Name the seams in writing with a rule each, rather than redrawing boundaries until the argument disappears, because it will not.
terms.text: The boundary between two domains where responsibility is genuinely contested - the invoice, consent, stock in transit. Name the seams in writing with a rule each, rather than redrawing boundaries until the argument disappears, because it will not.

terms.html: The layer covering identity, access, data protection, and the controls that make the rest defensible. Best treated as a design input from day one rather than a review at the end, because retrofitting it is always the expensive path.
terms.text: The layer covering identity, access, data protection, and the controls that make the rest defensible. Best treated as a design input from day one rather than a review at the end, because retrofitting it is always the expensive path.

terms.html: Architecture scoped to one slice of the enterprise - a domain, a market, a value stream - detailed enough to guide projects within it. Where the useful middle ground between an enterprise map and a solution design lives.
terms.text: Architecture scoped to one slice of the enterprise - a domain, a market, a value stream - detailed enough to guide projects within it. Where the useful middle ground between an enterprise map and a solution design lives.

terms.html: Splitting a sensitive process so no single person can complete it alone. A control that architecture has to design for rather than bolt on, because it constrains workflow rather than just access.
terms.text: Splitting a sensitive process so no single person can complete it alone. A control that architecture has to design for rather than bolt on, because it constrains workflow rather than just access.

terms.html: A committed level of service with consequences attached. Without the consequences it is a target, and targets are what get missed quietly.
terms.text: A committed level of service with consequences attached. Without the consequences it is a target, and targets are what get missed quietly.

terms.html: Infrastructure that handles service-to-service communication concerns - discovery, retries, encryption, telemetry - outside application code. Solves real problems and adds an operational surface most teams underestimate.
terms.text: Infrastructure that handles service-to-service communication concerns - discovery, retries, encryption, telemetry - outside application code. Solves real problems and adds an operational surface most teams underestimate.

terms.html: Systems acquired and run outside IT's knowledge - usually a spreadsheet that grew teeth, or a SaaS subscription on a corporate card. Less a compliance sin than a signal: somewhere, a real need went unserved.
terms.text: Systems acquired and run outside IT's knowledge - usually a spreadsheet that grew teeth, or a SaaS subscription on a corporate card. Less a compliance sin than a signal: somewhere, a real need went unserved.

terms.html: A service you own, in your own runtime, talking to the packaged core through published contracts. Where anything substantial belongs, and the reason an upgrade stays a weekend.
terms.text: A service you own, in your own runtime, talking to the packaged core through published contracts. Where anything substantial belongs, and the reason an upgrade stays a weekend.

terms.html: One authentication that grants access to many systems. The highest-value integration most organizations can do for user experience and for security at the same time.
terms.text: One authentication that grants access to many systems. The highest-value integration most organizations can do for user experience and for security at the same time.

terms.html: The set of options for moving an application to a new platform: retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, replace. A useful vocabulary for a migration, and an excellent way to discover that half the estate should be retired.
terms.text: The set of options for moving an application to a new platform: retain, retire, rehost, replatform, refactor, replace. A useful vocabulary for a migration, and an excellent way to discover that half the estate should be retired.

terms.html: Software operated by the vendor and consumed as a subscription. It removes the operations problem and sharpens every other one: integration, data residency, exit, and the fact that the roadmap is no longer yours.
terms.text: Software operated by the vendor and consumed as a subscription. It removes the operations problem and sharpens every other one: integration, data residency, exit, and the fact that the roadmap is no longer yours.

terms.html: Architecture practiced at the level of one project or product: the concrete design that has to work by the go-live date. Good solution architects translate enterprise intention into something that ships.
terms.text: Architecture practiced at the level of one project or product: the concrete design that has to work by the go-live date. Good solution architects translate enterprise intention into something that ships.

terms.html: A decision point in the delivery lifecycle where a project must show something to continue. Architecture adds a field, a reviewer, or an exit condition to these, never a gate of its own.
terms.text: A decision point in the delivery lifecycle where a project must show something to continue. Architecture adds a field, a reviewer, or an exit condition to these, never a gate of its own.

terms.html: Anyone whose decisions the architecture affects or who can affect the architecture. The list is always longer than the invitation list, which is the source of most late surprises.
terms.text: Anyone whose decisions the architecture affects or who can affect the architecture. The list is always longer than the invitation list, which is the source of most late surprises.

terms.html: A technology or pattern the organization has committed to, with an owner and a review date. An active standard shortens a hundred future discussions; an unmaintained one is nostalgia with authority.
terms.text: A technology or pattern the organization has committed to, with an owner and a review date. An active standard shortens a hundred future discussions; an unmaintained one is nostalgia with authority.

terms.html: The document defining what a supplier will deliver, by when, and for how much. Anything promised during evaluation and not written here did not happen.
terms.text: The document defining what a supplier will deliver, by when, and for how much. Anything promised during evaluation and not written here did not happen.

terms.html: Something the law or a regulator requires, distinguishable from a preference by having a source outside the person describing it. Smaller than everyone expects, and worth checking against the vendor's country versions before building anything.
terms.text: Something the law or a regulator requires, distinguishable from a preference by having a source outside the person describing it. Smaller than everyone expects, and worth checking against the vendor's country versions before building anything.

terms.html: The senior forum that funds and prioritizes a programme. It decides money and sequence; if it is deciding designs, something below it has stopped working.
terms.text: The senior forum that funds and prioritizes a programme. It decides money and sequence; if it is deciding designs, something below it has stopped working.

terms.html: A migration pattern where new functionality is built around a legacy system until the old one can be removed. It works, and it only finishes if somebody keeps a list of what is left and a date against it.
terms.text: A migration pattern where new functionality is built around a legacy system until the old one can be removed. It works, and it only finishes if somebody keeps a list of what is left and a date against it.

terms.html: The principle that decisions should be taken at the most local level capable of taking them, with higher levels handling only what the local level cannot. The best architectural rule for a federation, and one that predates computing by a long way.
terms.text: The principle that decisions should be taken at the most local level capable of taking them, with higher levels handling only what the local level cannot. The best architectural rule for a federation, and one that predates computing by a long way.

terms.html: The agreed date on which a system stops being used. A phase-out state without a date is an intention; with a date it is a plan, and only one of the two ever happens.
terms.text: The agreed date on which a system stops being used. A phase-out state without a date is an intention; with a date it is a plan, and only one of the two ever happens.

terms.html: Exchange where the caller blocks until the other side answers. Every one of these is a coupling: when the other system is down or upgrading, so are you.
terms.text: Exchange where the caller blocks until the other side answers. Every one of these is a coupling: when the other system is down or upgrading, so are you.

terms.html: The one system that creates and changes a given object; everyone else consumes. Writing this down for each object is the single most consequential sentence in a data strategy and the one most often left out.
terms.text: The one system that creates and changes a given object; everyone else consumes. Writing this down for each object is the single most consequential sentence in a data strategy and the one most often left out.

terms.html: An authorized copy of an object held elsewhere for a stated purpose, ideally with an expiry date. The difference between a legitimate reference copy and a second master is whether anyone wrote the purpose down.
terms.text: An authorized copy of an object held elsewhere for a stated purpose, ideally with an expiry date. The difference between a legitimate reference copy and a second master is whether anyone wrote the purpose down.

terms.html: The intended future state of the operating model: which capabilities are centralized, which are local, and who decides what. Architecture that ignores it will produce systems the organization cannot staff.
terms.text: The intended future state of the operating model: which capabilities are centralized, which are local, and who decides what. Architecture that ignores it will produce systems the organization cannot staff.

terms.html: A hierarchical classification used to organize things consistently - a product taxonomy, a spend taxonomy. Cheap to define, expensive to change later, so it deserves more argument up front than it usually gets.
terms.text: A hierarchical classification used to organize things consistently - a product taxonomy, a spend taxonomy. Cheap to define, expensive to change later, so it deserves more argument up front than it usually gets.

terms.html: The accumulated cost of past shortcuts: systems kept alive too long, integrations built twice, documentation that lives in one person's head. Like financial debt, survivable when visible and serviced - fatal when denied.
terms.text: The accumulated cost of past shortcuts: systems kept alive too long, integrations built twice, documentation that lives in one person's head. Like financial debt, survivable when visible and serviced - fatal when denied.

terms.html: A rating of an application's technical health: currency of the stack, support status, integration debt, operability. Rated by IT, on a published scale, and never blended with business fit.
terms.text: A rating of an application's technical health: currency of the stack, support status, integration debt, operability. Rated by IT, on a published scale, and never blended with business fit.

terms.html: The layer covering platforms, runtimes, networks, and infrastructure - the substrate everything else runs on. Increasingly a set of purchasing and configuration decisions rather than engineering ones.
terms.text: The layer covering platforms, runtimes, networks, and infrastructure - the substrate everything else runs on. Increasingly a set of purchasing and configuration decisions rather than engineering ones.

terms.html: A published view of technologies the organization is adopting, trialling, holding, or retiring. Its value is not the picture, it is that somebody had to decide which ring each thing goes in.
terms.text: A published view of technologies the organization is adopting, trialling, holding, or retiring. Its value is not the picture, it is that somebody had to decide which ring each thing goes in.

terms.html: A specific technology the organization has committed to for a purpose, with an owner and a review date. Standards that nobody reviews become the reason new hires quietly install something else.
terms.text: A specific technology the organization has committed to for a purpose, with an owner and a review date. Standards that nobody reviews become the reason new hires quietly install something else.

terms.html: Deploying one agreed configuration across markets, adapting only where genuinely necessary. It works exactly as well as the honesty of the fit-gap triage that preceded it.
terms.text: Deploying one agreed configuration across markets, adapting only where genuinely necessary. It works exactly as well as the honesty of the fit-gap triage that preceded it.

terms.html: A structured look at what could go wrong, who would want it to, and what would stop them. An hour of it at design time is worth more than any amount of scanning afterwards.
terms.text: A structured look at what could go wrong, who would want it to, and what would stop them. An hour of it at design time is worth more than any amount of scanning afterwards.

terms.html: A four-way classification of applications as tolerate, invest, migrate, or eliminate, based on business and technical fit. Its virtue is that it converts two ratings into one decision without hiding either of them.
terms.text: A four-way classification of applications as tolerate, invest, migrate, or eliminate, based on business and technical fit. Its virtue is that it converts two ratings into one decision without hiding either of them.

terms.html: A widely used enterprise architecture framework, best known for its Architecture Development Method. Valuable as a shared vocabulary and a checklist of things not to forget; dangerous when followed as a project plan.
terms.text: A widely used enterprise architecture framework, best known for its Architecture Development Method. Valuable as a shared vocabulary and a checklist of things not to forget; dangerous when followed as a project plan.

terms.html: Everything a system costs over its life: licences, infrastructure, support, integration, and the people who keep it alive. The last item is the one always missing from the business case.
terms.text: Everything a system costs over its life: licences, infrastructure, support, integration, and the people who keep it alive. The last item is the one always missing from the business case.

terms.html: Following a single request across the services it touches. The mechanism that makes distributed systems debuggable, and the thing teams wish they had added before the first bad incident.
terms.text: Following a single request across the services it touches. The mechanism that makes distributed systems debuggable, and the thing teams wish they had added before the first bad incident.

terms.html: The records of things that happened: orders, movements, payments. High volume, short-lived relevance, and the reason master data quality problems become visible at scale.
terms.text: The records of things that happened: orders, movements, payments. High volume, short-lived relevance, and the reason master data quality problems become visible at scale.

terms.html: A deliberate intermediate state between baseline and target - the bridge you operate while a program lands. Flagging systems as transition states keeps churn from being mistaken for bad data.
terms.text: A deliberate intermediate state between baseline and target - the bridge you operate while a program lands. Flagging systems as transition states keeps churn from being mistaken for bad data.

terms.html: A model with exactly two checkpoints - a direction check before design and a design check before build - with an engineer-level forum underneath. Enough governance to catch misfits, little enough that projects still show up.
terms.text: A model with exactly two checkpoints - a direction check before design and a design check before build - with an engineer-level forum underneath. Enough governance to catch misfits, little enough that projects still show up.

terms.html: The route from your current version of a packaged system to the next one. A programme that has never rehearsed an upgrade does not know whether its core is clean; it knows whether its rules were followed, which is not the same thing.
terms.text: The route from your current version of a packaged system to the next one. A programme that has never rehearsed an upgrade does not know whether its core is clean; it knows whether its rules were followed, which is not the same thing.

terms.html: The sequence of activities through which an organization creates value, from supply to customer. Older framing than value streams and still the fastest way to explain a business to somebody in ten minutes.
terms.text: The sequence of activities through which an organization creates value, from supply to customer. Older framing than value streams and still the fastest way to explain a business to somebody in ten minutes.

terms.html: The end-to-end set of steps that delivers a result to a stakeholder, cutting across functions. Mapping one is the quickest way to find the four handovers where the work waits.
terms.text: The end-to-end set of steps that delivers a result to a stakeholder, cutting across functions. Mapping one is the quickest way to find the four handovers where the work waits.

terms.html: The cost of leaving a supplier, measured in data extraction, retraining, and reintegration. Never zero, frequently acceptable, and always cheaper to negotiate down before signature than to complain about afterwards.
terms.text: The cost of leaving a supplier, measured in data extraction, retraining, and reintegration. Never zero, frequently acceptable, and always cheaper to negotiate down before signature than to complain about afterwards.

terms.html: The process of choosing a supplier against published criteria. Architecture criteria at ten per cent of the total score are a rounding error with a seat at the table; one mandatory criterion is worth more than five points of weight.
terms.text: The process of choosing a supplier against published criteria. Architecture criteria at ten per cent of the total score are a rounding error with a seat at the table; one mandatory criterion is worth more than five points of weight.

terms.html: Publishing changes to an interface in a way that lets consumers move at their own pace. A stated deprecation notice period is worth more to a consumer than any amount of goodwill.
terms.text: Publishing changes to an interface in a way that lets consumers move at their own pace. A stated deprecation notice period is worth more to a consumer than any amount of goodwill.

terms.html: A representation of the architecture aimed at one audience and one set of concerns - a landscape diagram for executives, a sequence diagram for engineers. A view that serves two audiences usually serves neither.
terms.text: A representation of the architecture aimed at one audience and one set of concerns - a landscape diagram for executives, a sequence diagram for engineers. A view that serves two audiences usually serves neither.

terms.html: The rules for building a particular kind of view: what is shown, what is left out, and for whom. Agreeing viewpoints once saves an argument about diagram conventions in every single review.
terms.text: The rules for building a particular kind of view: what is shown, what is left out, and for whom. Agreeing viewpoints once saves an argument about diagram conventions in every single review.

terms.html: A short, protected place on a governance agenda for someone who is not a member but is affected. It converts the people most likely to route around the board into the people who asked to attend.
terms.text: A short, protected place on a governance agenda for someone who is not a member but is affected. It converts the people most likely to route around the board into the people who asked to attend.

terms.html: Formal permission to not comply, usually granted above the level that set the rule. Distinct from an exception in that a waiver rarely carries an expiry, which is precisely why it should.
terms.text: Formal permission to not comply, usually granted above the level that set the rule. Distinct from an exception in that a waiver rarely carries an expiry, which is precisely why it should.

terms.html: A map that positions components by value-chain visibility and by evolutionary maturity, from genesis to commodity. Its practical use is arguing about what to build versus buy with something other than instinct.
terms.text: A map that positions components by value-chain visibility and by evolutionary maturity, from genesis to commodity. Its practical use is arguing about what to build versus buy with something other than instinct.

terms.html: One planned slice of a rollout or transformation - a set of domains, markets, or systems moved together. Waves make multi-year change survivable: while one wave lands, the next is being designed.
terms.text: One planned slice of a rollout or transformation - a set of domains, markets, or systems moved together. Waves make multi-year change survivable: while one wave lands, the next is being designed.

terms.html: An outbound HTTP call a system makes when something happens, so consumers do not have to poll. Cheap, effective, and only as reliable as its retry policy.
terms.text: An outbound HTTP call a system makes when something happens, so consumers do not have to poll. Cheap, effective, and only as reliable as its retry policy.

terms.html: A classification scheme that crosses six questions (what, how, where, who, when, why) with six perspectives, producing a grid of architecture artifacts. More useful as a completeness check than as a work plan.
terms.text: A classification scheme that crosses six questions (what, how, where, who, when, why) with six perspectives, producing a grid of architecture artifacts. More useful as a completeness check than as a work plan.

terms.html: A security model that assumes no network location is inherently trusted and verifies every request. Sound as a direction and frequently sold as a product, which are two different purchases.
terms.text: A security model that assumes no network location is inherently trusted and verifies every request. Sound as a direction and frequently sold as a product, which are two different purchases.

terms.html: A system that is operationally alive but organizationally dead: no owner, no roadmap, no one who dares to switch it off. Every landscape has a few; mature portfolios know their names.
